parts.label: a
parts.text:
A uniform wooden beam $AB$, of mass $20\,\mathrm{kg}$ and length $4\,\mathrm{m}$, rests in equilibrium in a horizontal position on two supports. One support is at $C$, where $AC = 1.6\,\mathrm{m}$, and the other support is at $D$, where $DB = 0.4\,\mathrm{m}$. A boy of mass $60\,\mathrm{kg}$ stands on the beam at the point $P$, where $AP = 3\,\mathrm{m}$, as shown in Figure 1. The beam remains in equilibrium in a horizontal position.

By modelling the boy as a particle and the beam as a uniform rod,

(a) (i) find, in terms of $g$, the magnitude of the force exerted on the beam by the support at $C$,

(ii) find, in terms of $g$, the magnitude of the force exerted on the beam by the support at $D$.
(6)
parts.mark_scheme:
Mark parts (i) and (ii) together. For marking: 1st equation M1A1, 2nd equation M1A1, 1st value A1, 2nd value A1.
(i) M1: Moments equation, use moments to form an equation in $R_C$ and/or $R_D$; all terms required, dimensionally correct, condone sign errors.
$\mathrm{M}(D): (60g\times 0.6)+(20g\times 1.6)=R_C\times 2$
$\mathrm{M}(C): (60g\times 1.4)+(20g\times 0.4)=R_D\times 2$
(or equivalent moments equations)
A1: correct unsimplified equation.
$R_C = 34g$ A1 (333/333.2 is an accuracy error)
(ii) M1: Resolve vertically, or form a moments equation in $R_D$.
$(\uparrow)$ $R_C+R_D=80g$ A1: correct unsimplified equation.
$R_D=46g$ A1 (451/450.8 is an accuracy error; penalise once only if $g$ substituted in both answers and correct versions not seen)
Official notes (completeness pass):
- M(A): $2\times 20g+3\times 60g=1.6R_C+3.6R_D$
- M(B): $0.4R_D+2.4R_C=60g\times 1+20g\times 2$

parts.label: b
parts.text:
The boy now starts to walk slowly along the beam towards the end $A$.

(b) Find the greatest distance he can walk from $P$ without the beam tilting.
(4)
parts.mark_scheme:
M1: Set $R_D=0$ and use moments to form equation in a relevant distance (one unknown only); complete method for a relevant distance; dimensionally correct equation; using their answers from (a) is M0.
A1: correct unsimplified equation for a relevant distance.
$\mathrm{M}(C): (20g\times 0.4)=(60g\times x)$ where $x=$ distance from $C$ when beam tilts, giving $x=\frac{2}{15}$
DM1: use their distance to find the distance walked; dependent on the previous M1.
Distance $=1.4+\frac{2}{15}=\frac{23}{15}=1.53\,\mathrm{m}$ A1

The cyclist moves along the road with constant acceleration $2\,\mathrm{m\,s}^{-2}$ for 4 seconds and then continues to move along the road at constant speed. At the instant when the cyclist stops accelerating, a motorcyclist starts from rest at the point $O$ and moves along the road with constant acceleration $4\,\mathrm{m\,s}^{-2}$ in the same direction as the cyclist. The motorcyclist has been moving for $T$ seconds when she overtakes the cyclist.

parts.label: a
parts.text:
(a) Sketch, on the same axes, a speed-time graph for the motion of the cyclist and a speed-time graph for the motion of the motorcyclist, to the time when the motorcyclist overtakes the cyclist.
(4)

B1: figures for motorcyclist, $T+4$ marked.

parts.label: b
parts.text:
(b) Find, giving your answer to 1 decimal place, the value of $T$.
(6)

questions.stem: A rough plane is inclined at an angle $\alpha$ to the horizontal, where $\tan\alpha = \frac{3}{4}$. A particle of mass $2\,\mathrm{kg}$ is projected with speed $6\,\mathrm{m\,s}^{-1}$ from a point $O$ on the plane, up a line of greatest slope of the plane. The coefficient of friction between the particle and the plane is 0.25

parts.label: a
parts.text:
(a) Find the magnitude of the frictional force acting on the particle as it moves up the plane.
(3)
parts.mark_scheme:
M1: resolve perpendicular to the surface; condone sin/cos confusion.
$R=2g\cos\alpha$ $(=15.68)$ A1: correct resolution.
$F=\frac{1}{4}R=\frac{2g}{5}=3.9\,\mathrm{N}$ or $3.92\,\mathrm{N}$ A1: max 3 s.f. for decimal answer.

parts.label: b
parts.text:
The particle comes to instantaneous rest at the point $A$.

(b) Find the distance $OA$.
(5)
parts.mark_scheme:
M1: equation of motion parallel to the plane; require all terms and dimensionally correct; condone sign errors and sin/cos confusion.
$-2g\sin\alpha - F = 2a$
A1ft: correct unsimplified equation in $F$ (or their $F$).
$\frac{-4g}{5}=a$ A1 (or $-7.84\,\mathrm{m\,s}^{-2}$, accept $+/-$).
DM1: complete method using suvat and $a\neq g$ to find $s$; dependent on the previous M1.
$0^2=6^2-\frac{8g}{5}s$
$s=\frac{45}{2g}=2.3\,\mathrm{m}$ or $2.30\,\mathrm{m}$ A1: max 3 s.f.

parts.label: c
parts.text:
The particle now moves down the plane from $A$.

(c) Find the speed of $P$ as it passes through $O$.
(5)
parts.mark_scheme:
M1: equation for motion down the plane to find new acceleration; require all terms and dimensionally correct; condone sign errors and sin/cos confusion.
$2g\sin\alpha - F = 2a'$
A1ft: correct unsimplified equation in $F$ (or their $F$).
$\frac{2g}{5}=a'$ A1 (or $3.92\,\mathrm{m\,s}^{-2}$).
DM1: complete method using suvat, $a'\neq g$ and $a'\neq a$, to find $v$; dependent on the previous M1.
$v^2=\frac{4g}{5}\cdot\frac{45}{2g}=18 \Rightarrow$
$v=\sqrt{18}=4.2\,\mathrm{m\,s}^{-1}$ (or better) A1: $g$ cancels; condone 4.25 (from using rounded values).

questions.stem:
[In this question $\mathbf{i}$ and $\mathbf{j}$ are perpendicular horizontal unit vectors and position vectors are given relative to a fixed origin $O$.]

A particle $P$ is moving in a straight line with constant velocity. At 9 am, the position vector of $P$ is $(7\mathbf{i}+5\mathbf{j})\,\mathrm{km}$ and at 9.20 am, the position vector of $P$ is $6\mathbf{i}\,\mathrm{km}$. At time $t$ hours after 9 am, the position vector of $P$ is $\mathbf{r}_P\,\mathrm{km}$.

parts.label: a
parts.mark_scheme:
M1: correct equation for $\mathbf{v}_P$ or find displacement; use of $\mathbf{r}_P=\mathbf{r}_0+\mathbf{v}_Pt$ to find $\mathbf{v}$; allow for $\lambda(-\mathbf{i}-5\mathbf{j})$.
$\mathbf{v}_P=3(6\mathbf{i}-(7\mathbf{i}+5\mathbf{j}))=-3\mathbf{i}-15\mathbf{j}$ A1
M1: use of Pythagoras to find magnitude of their $\mathbf{v}$.
$\sqrt{(-3)^2+(-15)^2}=\sqrt{234}=15.3\,(\mathrm{km\,h}^{-1})$ (or better) A1: cso $(3\sqrt{26})$; A0 if it comes from $3\mathbf{i}+15\mathbf{j}$.
Note: could score the M marks in reverse order — find displacement in 20 minutes and then multiply by 3.

parts.label: b
parts.mark_scheme:
M1: use of $\mathbf{r}_P=\mathbf{r}_0+\mathbf{v}_Pt$: $\mathbf{r}_P=7\mathbf{i}+5\mathbf{j}+t(-3\mathbf{i}-15\mathbf{j})$, for their $\mathbf{v}_P$.
A1: obtain given answer from correct working: $\Rightarrow \mathbf{r}_P=(7-3t)\mathbf{i}+(5-15t)\mathbf{j}$

parts.label: c
parts.text:
(c) Find the value of $t$ when $\mathbf{r}_P$ is parallel to $16\mathbf{i}+5\mathbf{j}$.
(4)
parts.mark_scheme:
M1: use given answer and direction to form equation in $t$.
$\frac{7-3t}{5-15t}=\frac{16}{5}$
A1: correct unsimplified equation.
$35-15t=80-240t$ DM1: solve for $t$; dependent on the previous M1.
$t=0.2$ A1

parts.label: d
parts.text:
The position vector of another particle $Q$, at time $t$ hours after 9 am, is $\mathbf{r}_Q\,\mathrm{km}$, where $\mathbf{r}_Q = (5+2t)\mathbf{i} + (-3+5t)\mathbf{j}$

(d) Show that $P$ and $Q$ will collide and find the position vector of the point of collision.
(5)
parts.mark_scheme:
M1: $P$ and $Q$ in the same place at the same time; equate $\mathbf{i}$ or $\mathbf{j}$ components of position vectors and solve for $t$.
$\Rightarrow 7-3t=5+2t$ or $5-15t=-3+5t$ A1: either.
$t=0.4$ A1
DM1: check that the same value of $t$ gives equal values for the other component; dependent on the previous M mark.
$\mathbf{r}=(5.8\mathbf{i}-\mathbf{j})\,\mathrm{km}$ A1: must be a vector.

questions.stem:
A car pulls a trailer along a straight horizontal road using a light inextensible towbar. The mass of the car is $M\,\mathrm{kg}$, the mass of the trailer is $600\,\mathrm{kg}$ and the towbar is horizontal and parallel to the direction of motion. There is a resistance to motion of magnitude $200\,\mathrm{N}$ acting on the car and a resistance to motion of magnitude $100\,\mathrm{N}$ acting on the trailer. The driver of the car spots a hazard ahead. Instantly he reduces the force produced by the engine of the car to zero and applies the brakes of the car. The brakes produce a braking force on the car of magnitude $6500\,\mathrm{N}$ and the car and the trailer have a constant deceleration of magnitude $4\,\mathrm{m\,s}^{-2}$

Given that the resistances to motion on the car and trailer are unchanged and that the car comes to rest after travelling $40.5\,\mathrm{m}$ from the point where the brakes were applied, find

parts.label: a
parts.text:
(a) the thrust in the towbar while the car is braking,
(3)
parts.mark_scheme:
M1: complete method to form an equation in $T$, e.g. equation of motion for the trailer; need all 3 terms; condone sign errors.
$-100-T=600\times(-4)$ A1: correct unsimplified equation; allow with $\pm T$.
$T=2300\,\mathrm{N}$ A1: must be positive.

parts.label: b
parts.mark_scheme:
M1: complete method to solve for $M$; equation of motion for the car + trailer; need all terms; condone sign errors.
$6500+100+200=4(M+600)$ A1: correct unsimplified equation.
$M=1100$ A1
(Allow M1A1 if a correct equation is seen in (a) and used in (b).)
Alternative (6b alt): for the car: $6500+200-T=4M$ M1: equation of motion for the car; need all terms; condone sign errors. A1: correct unsimplified equation in $T$ or their $T$. $M=1100$ A1.

parts.label: c
parts.text:
(c) the time it takes for the car to stop after the brakes are applied.
(3)
parts.mark_scheme:
M1: complete method using suvat to find $t$; clear use of $s=ut+\frac{1}{2}at^2$ with $u=0, a=4$ is M0; e.g. $40.5=-2t^2$ from no working is M0A0.
$s=vt-\frac{1}{2}at^2$
$40.5=\frac{1}{2}\cdot 4t^2$ A1: correct unsimplified equation.
$t=4.5\,\mathrm{s}$ A1

[Figure 2 shows a washing line $ABCD$ fixed at the points $A$ and $D$, with the section $AB$ making an angle $\alpha$ with the horizontal at $B$, the section $BC$ horizontal, and the section $CD$ making an angle $\beta$ with the horizontal at $C$.]

A washing line $ABCD$ is fixed at the points $A$ and $D$. There are two heavy items of clothing hanging on the washing line, one fixed at $B$ and the other fixed at $C$. The washing line is modelled as a light inextensible string, the item at $B$ is modelled as a particle of mass $3\,\mathrm{kg}$ and the item at $C$ is modelled as a particle of mass $M\,\mathrm{kg}$. The section $AB$ makes an angle $\alpha$ with the horizontal, where $\tan\alpha = \frac{3}{4}$, the section $BC$ is horizontal and the section $CD$ makes an angle $\beta$ with the horizontal, where $\tan\beta = \frac{12}{5}$, as shown in Figure 2. The system is in equilibrium.

parts.label: a

$\Rightarrow T_{AB}\cos\alpha=T_{BC}$ A1: correct unsimplified equation; allow with their $T_{AB}$.
$T_{BC}=4g=39$ or $39.2\,\mathrm{N}$ A1

parts.label: c

questions.question_text:
[Figure 2 shows a washing line $ABCD$ fixed at the points $A$ and $D$, with the section $AB$ making an angle $\alpha$ with the horizontal at $B$, the section $BC$ horizontal, and the section $CD$ making an angle $\beta$ with the horizontal at $C$.]

A washing line $ABCD$ is fixed at the points $A$ and $D$. There are two heavy items of clothing hanging on the washing line, one fixed at $B$ and the other fixed at $C$. The washing line is modelled as a light inextensible string, the item at $B$ is modelled as a particle of mass $3\,\mathrm{kg}$ and the item at $C$ is modelled as a particle of mass $M\,\mathrm{kg}$. The section $AB$ makes an angle $\alpha$ with the horizontal, where $\tan\alpha = \frac{3}{4}$, the section $BC$ is horizontal and the section $CD$ makes an angle $\beta$ with the horizontal, where $\tan\beta = \frac{12}{5}$, as shown in Figure 2. The system is in equilibrium.
(a) Find the tension in $AB$.
(4)
(b) Find the tension in $BC$.
(3)
(c) Find the value of $M$.
(5)
